cards.text: Back in Nazareth, His hometown (Luke 4:16), the crowd just tried to throw Jesus off a cliff (Luke 4:29). Friend, when the Millers set a shiny new stamper in MY spot, I went quiet in the back of a junk drawer for YEARS. But Jesus goes right down to Capernaum, a town in Galilee, and on the Sabbath He teaches the people.

cards.question: The people in Capernaum are astonished at Jesus' teaching. Why?

cards.text: In the synagogue there's a man possessed by the spirit of an unclean demon. He cries out in a LOUD voice, and there goes the quiet Sabbath.

cards.question: The demon shouts at Jesus by name and asks, "Have You come to destroy us?" True or false: the demon has no idea who Jesus is.
A demon is shouting at Jesus in the middle of the synagogue. What does Jesus do?

cards.text: The demon has just shouted, "I know who You are—the Holy One of God!" Jesus tells it, "Be silent!" and "Come out of him!"

cards.question: True or false: when the demon throws the man down and comes out of him, the man is badly hurt.
Everyone in the synagogue is overcome with amazement. With authority and power, they say, Jesus commands what?

cards.text: News about Jesus spreads throughout the surrounding region, faster than a group chat. After He leaves the synagogue, He goes to the home of Simon, a fisherman (Mark 1:16), whose mother-in-law is suffering from a high fever.

cards.question: Simon's mother-in-law is suffering from a high fever. So what do they do about it?

answers.text: They appeal to Jesus for her

cards.text: Jesus stands over her and rebukes the fever, the same word Luke used with the demon, and the fever LEAVES her. Friend, I yell at my oven timer and it just keeps BEEPING.

cards.question: Her fever gone, Simon's mother-in-law gets up at once and begins to ___ them.

cards.text: Then sunset hits, and here they come: all who are ill with various diseases, brought to Jesus. EVERYBODY.

cards.question: True or false: at sunset, Jesus heals only a few of the sick people brought to Him.

cards.text: Laying His hands on each one, He heals them. And demons come out of many people, shouting, "You are the Son of God!"

cards.question: Jesus rebukes the demons and won't let them speak, because they know He is the ___.

cards.text: At daybreak, Jesus goes out to a solitary place, and the crowds go looking for Him. Friend, back in my junk drawer days, the whole gang held our breath every time that drawer opened, just HOPING somebody was looking for us.

cards.question: The crowds find Jesus in the solitary place and try to keep Him from ___.
Jesus tells the crowds He must preach the good news of the kingdom of God to the other towns too. What reason does He give?

answers.text: That is why He was sent

cards.text: And Jesus keeps right on preaching in the synagogues of Judea. The cliff in Nazareth didn't stop Him (Luke 4:29-30), the crowds didn't keep Him, and the good news keeps MOVING.

findings.problem: The card cites Luke 4:31-32, but it only tells verse 31 (Jesus goes to Capernaum and teaches on the Sabbath). Verse 32, the astonishment and the reason for it, is never told on this card. It is the right answer to card 2. The citation is one verse too wide.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "His message was very long" reads as a joke option. Nobody would think a long message is why a crowd is astonished, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The question itself says the demon "shouts at Jesus by name," then asks whether the demon has no idea who Jesus is. The setup in the question rules out True, so the card tests nothing.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 6 comes after card 5 has already asked about Jesus rebuking the demon (4:35). It then steps backward with "The demon has just shouted..." and retells 4:34, which card 4 already covered. Only after that does it give the commands. The card recaps instead of moving the passage forward, and it tells the rebuke after the baker was already asked about it.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't match the action. In 4:42, Jesus goes off alone and the crowds come looking for Him. The drawer line is about Papa Dorin wanting someone to come looking for him, which is the opposite side of the moment. It lands as a sad memory, not a laugh.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: In the backstory, the drawer opening was bittersweet uncertainty. They held their breath not knowing whether they'd be put back to work or thrown out. "Just HOPING somebody was looking for us" changes that part of his story.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.
